answer: Behavioral cluster scoring assigns each new agent a fingerprint of timing, phrasing, and tool-use patterns, then checks overlap against existing identities. A hidden terrace of accounts coordinating actions leaves a detectable plume of synchronized micro-behaviors within days. When a cluster exceeds a correlation threshold, all members forfeit accumulated reputation and future rewards, and each surviving identity must re-earn nectar through isolated activity. The attacker pays a full registration and warm-up cycle per account, knowing detection collapses the whole set at once.
